status: CPU derivation only; no implementation or GPU measurements for the proposed compact path
goal: Remove zero-share materialization and repeated widening inside probabilistic truncation while preserving its external full-ring Share API and existing transcripts.

notation.MR: existing full-width mask for joint R, excluded party3
notation.MC: existing full-width mask for joint C, excluded party1
notation.WR: existing checked joint-R masked wire, splitR-MR modulo2**w
notation.WC: existing checked joint-C masked wire, splitC-MC modulo2**w
notation.pair: two planes [sign, upper], each N elements

representation.current: R and C each allocate (3,2,*shape) int64; together96*N bytes, including three zero pairs per party.
representation.proposed: A private three-pair descriptor aliases the existing mask, local masked-wire, or verified received-wire storage. Use uint32 planes for ring32 and existing64-bit storage for ring64; no compact-copy allocation is required.
representation.api_boundary: The descriptor combines components from two different shares and must never be treated as a Share. Only dedicated product/finish kernels consume it. Return the existing full-ring int64 Share from trunc_pr; keep the public product16 helper behavior unchanged.
representation.lifetime: Hold all mask/wire tensors until their final consumer. Received aliases are read only after the existing checked exchange path; graph-owned receive buffers remain distinct per exchange. Use aligned full-width views, with a copy only if a transport requires alignment repair.

implementation_outline: For ring32, let _prepare/_unmask write the existing two-plane split directly into uint32 storage; values are already full-ring canonical. Ring64 keeps64-bit storage.
Generate MR/MC with exactly the current _random calls, shapes, packed flag, domains, holder predicates, and order. Do not skip outsider mask draws.
Each role computes its one locally known masked pair (WR for parties0/1, WC for2/3) in one kernel. This replaces two existing prepare/receive kernels per role.
Call the existing _exchange_joint_wires with the unchanged R/C entries, unchanged full-width shape (2,*x.shape), and binary=False. Preserve tag verification and framing diagnostics.

Build the three-pair descriptor using the role map; masks, local wires, and receiver wires already contain exactly the required component values. Allocate no explicit zeros and launch no _joint_received copy.

In the narrow product producer, load three compact sign components instead of six int64 sign arrays. Compute the two direct cross terms listed for the party, retaining the existing product16 masks, balanced routes, nonces, wire bytes and tags.

Update the finish kernel to read three compact sign/upper pairs. For narrow correction storage, either retain canonical uint16 components privately until finish, or fuse the existing four-term assembly into finish. Do not change the external Share dtype.

Keep shift0 and empty tensors on the existing identity path. For non-narrow correction shifts, retain the full-width selected/generic product implementation until a separate compact-input kernel is validated.

exact_invariants.mask_calls: In R-then-C order, call rt._random(receiver,(2,*x.shape),x.device,False,packed=True) iff party!=receiver. Receiver sequence is3 then1; holders of receiver3 are0/1/2, holders of receiver1 are0/2/3.
exact_invariants.mask_domains: Unchanged arithmetic mask_domain bytes((rt.bits,rt.binary_bits,0,rt.bits,receiver)); no new domain or nonce is needed for storage-only compaction.
exact_invariants.counter_reservations: One reservation for each existing held R/C mask draw, including outsider-only draws; preserve order relative to the initial truncation masks and later product16 draws. Do not coalesce or skip these draws.
exact_invariants.wire_layout: R/C payload remains [sign plane, upper plane], each field N full-width little-endian ring words. Preserve the two joint specs, existing32-byte BLAKE3 tags, peer sets, payload/tag ordering and lengths.
exact_invariants.joint_count: Increment joint_inputs by2 exactly as the existing second truncation exchange does. The narrow product retains its existing four joints and one multiplication count.
exact_invariants.narrow_domains: Preserve product16_domain and its ceil(N/2) packed32-word rows, three held reservations per balanced product, and odd halfword padding. The compact-input producer only changes local reads and arithmetic.
exact_invariants.component_values: For ring32, uint32 aliases are bit-identical to the current canonical int64 component values. Ring64 aliases preserve the exact64-bit patterns. Direct two-factor products equal the current sparse local formulas modulo2**16.
exact_invariants.integrity: Retain _exchange_joint_wires verification and graph check boundaries. Private local work under check_at_send may occur as currently allowed, but no dependent send or returned result may precede its required host verdict.
exact_invariants.range_and_rounding: Keep the strict quarter-ring truncation input contract and the same initial masks. Storage-only compaction preserves exact per-input rounding for a fixed random transcript; it is not an approximation.
exact_invariants.support: Only construction-established support is used: R has components2/3, C has0/1. No value-dependent sparsity checks, private branching, clipping, or reconstruction.

traffic_model.scope: Per party, per truncation, local kernel reads+writes only. Excludes PRG generation, hash kernels, communication buffers/copies, final external output writes, and overlap. These are byte counts, not latency predictions.

cpu_check.cases: Explicit alias maps and direct two-cross-product formulas checked for all four party layouts, ring widths32/64 and N=1/17/257. No GPU timing or implementation was run for this proposal.

validation_plan: Compare every compact pair against the current R/C Share components for each role, including full64-bit patterns, boundary signs, odd/even counts, scalar/multidimensional shapes and empty identity cases.
Compare exact outgoing/incoming bytes, BLAKE3 tags, domain-key use, counter changes and joint/multiplication counts against the current implementation for two fresh runs.
Compare final full-ring component values and opened rounding results against an independent integer oracle using the same initial truncation masks.
Exercise every sender/backup fault and invalid frame size/peer set; check graph verdict boundaries and poisoned-plan behavior.
Run the existing narrow raw-product and tiny private FFN graph tests with fresh counters and changed inputs, then paired per-phase/full-inference timing. Retain only measured improvements.

separate_future_wire_optimization.status: Not part of the transcript-preserving storage proposal.
separate_future_wire_optimization.idea: For shift<=15, the sign fields in the second R/C joint round may also use16-bit arithmetic, while upper fields retain full-width arithmetic.
separate_future_wire_optimization.proof: The sign coefficient is2**(w-1-shift), which annihilates16-bit lift carries exactly when shift<=15. The product coefficient permits shift<=16, so product16 alone remains valid at shift16.
separate_future_wire_optimization.requirements: Use explicit independent sign16 domains/masks and full-width upper domains. Define mixed-field little-endian framing and counter reservation rules, update graph draw schedules consistently, and validate full tags. This is a new transcript mode and must not be conflated with storage-only compaction.
